title: Magnets
standard_code: Primary 2 Basic Science: You and Energy
standard_text: Magnets attract objects made of iron, steel and nickel; like poles repel and unlike poles attract; magnets are used in daily life. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 2, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): attraction and repulsion, magnetic materials, magnet strength and uses of magnets. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
body_html:
How to think about it

A magnet has a north pole and a south pole. When two magnets are brought together, unlike poles (north and south) attract and like poles (north and north) repel.

Magnets attract magnetic materials such as iron, steel and nickel, but not wood, plastic, paper, glass or aluminium. Magnetism can act through some materials. Magnets are used in refrigerator doors, compasses and speakers.

Example

Will a magnet attract a steel paper clip?

Steel contains iron.

Answer: yes

Example

Two north poles face each other. What happens?

Like poles

Answer: they repel

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all metals are attracted to magnets.
  • Thinking a bigger magnet is always stronger.
  • Thinking magnets only work when they touch.
